Goblins on this board. Those lines are deliberately shifted off the standard number: a Goblin is set easier and pays less, a Demon is set harder and pays more. A large gap against one is manufactured by the line, not evidence that the market is wrong. They were More-only until 21 August 2026, when PrizePicks began allowing Less on selected MLB and WNBA stat types (NFL followed in September). No PrizePicks page names the NBA yet, so a basketball Demon or Goblin may still offer More only. Which sides a line sells is read per line from your paste, and a row whose lean is not on offer is left out.
Reboot. PrizePicks voids a More pick on a full-game line if the player leaves in the first half and does not return, unless he already cleared it. The model does not price that yet, so More leans on bench roles carry more void risk than the lean suggests.
Model values are distribution medians for a player who plays, and the gap is median minus line in the stat's own units. Rows are ranked by measured reliability, then by how far the chance sits from a coin flip, never by the size of the gap. The posted line already carries almost everything a model knows, so read a gap as where the model disagrees, not as an edge: a leg has to hit 54.7% to 58.5% just to break even. Not betting advice.
